title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: No mathematical errors found. The presentation (2) is the correct amalgam presentation of GL(2,Z). τ'^2 = 1 holds with τ' = [[0,1],[1,0]]. τ(ρ) = σρ^{-1}σ^{-1} checks with τ = diag(1,-1) and ρ = [[1,-1],[1,0]].
The margin note is too fragmentary to verify. Its claims about τ' not respecting the Π̂_{0,3}^{{1,2}} structure cannot be checked from the page.
In (2), ρ^3 = σ^2 = -1 is imposed. The quotient map may identify more, but the statement is only that these relations hold, so this is fine.

ideas.what: Presentation of GL(2,Z) (hence of its profinite completion) by generators ρ, σ, τ' with ρ^6 = σ^4 = τ'^2 = 1, ρ^3 = σ^2, and τ' inverting ρ and σ; quotients of GL(2,Z)^ encoded as such triples in a profinite group.
ideas.modern_name: Amalgam decomposition GL(2,Z) ≅ D_4 *_{D_2} D_6; profinite completion of an amalgam
ideas.where_published: Not in this form; Esquisse d'un programme discusses SL(2,Z)/GL(2,Z) quotients and dessins in general terms

ideas.what: Choosing the involution τ' (normalising both <ρ> and <σ>) rather than τ = diag(1,-1) (inverting ε_0, ε_1) as the generator of the det = -1 part, with a discussion of the trade-off against compatibility with tangential base points on P^1 minus {0,1,∞}.
ideas.modern_name: Complex conjugation / orientation-reversing involution in Γ_{1,1}; compatibility with tangential base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in work on GT and Teichmüller towers (Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps)

ideas.what: Axiomatic setting: an arbitrary finite or profinite quotient 𝔾 of GL(2,Z)^ with 𝔾^+ the image of SL(2,Z)^, on which GT-type automorphism groups Z_{ρ,σ} are to be defined (next page).
ideas.modern_name: Finite-level / quotient versions of GT acting on Γ̂_{1,1}; GT-like groups for finite quotients
ideas.usually_credited_to: Related ideas: Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps (genus-one GT relation, 1990s); Nakamura; Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a general framework for GT-type automorphism groups attached to every finite quotient 𝔾 of GL(2,Z)^ (a groupoid/tower of 'Z_{ρ,σ}'-groups). This resembles a finite-level genus-one GT theory. Systematic treatments of GT at finite level exist mostly in genus 0, so this genus-one, quotient-by-quotient framework may be only partially explored.
missed.quote: Soit donc 𝔾 un groupe profini, muni d'un homomorphisme surjectif Γ̂^±_{1,1} ≃ Gl(2,Z)^ →épi 𝔾
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Finite-level GT-type groups attached to quotients of SL(2,Z)^ connect with modular dessins and Galois actions on non-congruence subgroups. A genus-one finite-level formalism could be compared with recent computational work on GT acting on finite quotients.

deep.surprise_reason: The page mostly fixes notation: the standard amalgam presentation of GL(2,Z) and a choice of involution. The only mildly interesting element is the intention to work with arbitrary finite quotients of GL(2,Z)^ in a genus-one GT setting, which is in line with known (if partly unpublished) directions.
transcription_corrections: The groups written T̂^±_{1,1} and T̂^+_{1,1} should be Γ̂_{1,1} (Γ̂^{±}_{1,1}, Γ̂^{+}_{1,1}), consistent with the previous page.
'10) Soit donc' should read '1°) Soit donc'; the next page continues with '2°)'.
'(ce qui des [?] est évidemment très vertueux !)' is more likely '(ce qui est évidemment très vertueux !)'.
'dont l'action sur ρ τ(ρ)=σ(ρ^{-1}) [?] commode' likely reads '... est moins commode'. Here σ(ρ^{-1}) means conjugation of ρ^{-1} by σ.

In the margin, 'Néanmoins, τ' a sur τ le désavantage de ne pas relever...' may be '...de ne pas respecter...'. The marginal note ends with 'De plus, τ' a ce désavantage d'être ...', and the heading below reads 'V Données préliminaires'.
